key_insight: In chaotic dynamical systems, distributional reinforcement learning can be better conditioned than standard expected-return RL because return distributions evolve more smoothly than individual trajectories under the 1-Wasserstein metric.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a more stable learning objective for control and decision-making in high-sensitivity domains such as fluid dynamics, climate modeling, and multi-agent systems.
method: Analyze RL in chaotic environments through the geometry of return distributions rather than scalar value estimates.
Use the 1-Wasserstein metric to characterize smoother evolution of return distributions under mild statistical stability assumptions.
Motivate distributional Bellman updates as a better-conditioned objective than expectation-based optimization.
evidence_signal: The paper provides a theoretical, abstract-level argument under mild statistical stability assumptions; no empirical dataset or benchmark results are stated in the abstract.
watch_item: The benefit depends on the stated statistical stability assumptions, so performance may degrade if the chaotic system or approximation scheme violates them.
paper_title: On Distributional Reinforcement Learning in Chaotic Dynamical Systems
